ratings.reason: Scriptwriting and audiovisual scene creation are clearly distinct production stages placed in a unified, synchronized workflow; synchronization strongly implies directly shared state. This is the strongest exemplar in the set. It names four interconnected workflow stages and makes shared state operational through forward and backward propagation of changes. Bidirectional propagation does more than co-locate tools: it resolves the difficult consistency problem created when upstream or downstream design decisions change. The mechanism is explicit and readily transferable to many staged workflows.
